info.title: Flowdeck
info.description: Manual testing as human flows. A test says what must be true; a flow says what a human does. Flowdeck integrates with nothing directly — it emits structured data and accepts structured data, and adapters written outside it decide what becomes a ticket.

actorHeader.name: X-Flowdeck-Actor
actorHeader.description: The name every write is attributed to. Not a secret and not authentication — Flowdeck is a name picker. Required on every write; ignored on reads.

delete.summary: Delete a product and everything in it
delete.description: Irreversible: tests, templates, runs, results and attachment records all go. Meant for wiping a product while an import script is still being debugged. Requires `?confirm=true`, since there is no undo and no archive at this level.

get.summary: List a product's tests
get.description: A flat searchable list. The feature-table grouping that mattered in a document is replaced by search and tags.

post.description: Returns the created tests in request order, which is what lets an importing script hold the mapping from its source rows to Flowdeck IDs. Import is knowingly not idempotent: running a parser twice creates everything twice.

201.description: The created tests, in request order

get.summary: Get a test at its current version

patch.summary: Edit a test — creates a new version
patch.description: The old version is never modified. Flows reference the test ID, so nothing needs repointing; that is the whole reason identity and versioning are separate.

200.description: The test at its new version

get.summary: Every version of a test, oldest first
get.description: The old version is never modified and never deleted, so a result recorded in March stays readable against March's wording after six edits.

get.summary: Coverage state for every test in a product
get.description: During a migration this is the progress bar: start with everything uncovered, finish when nothing is.

200.description: Coverage per test, plus the totals

post.description: Archiving stops the test counting toward coverage; existing marks render as 'archived test' and historical runs stay intact. Hard deletion is never offered — a test referenced in six flows and three runs cannot be safely erased.

200.description: The archived test, and how many places marked it

get.summary: List a product's templates
get.description: Several templates per product is the norm — one per setup. Archived templates are included, because they stop appearing in the run picker but keep counting toward coverage.

200.description: Templates with their flow and marked-test counts

post.summary: Bulk-create templates with their flows and steps
post.description: Phase two of an import. Steps reference tests by the IDs returned from phase one, so the importing script holds the mapping rather than Flowdeck knowing anything about the source.

get.summary: A template with its flows and steps

patch.summary: Rename, describe or archive a template
patch.description: Archived templates leave the 'start a testing day' picker but keep counting toward coverage.

delete.summary: Hard-delete a template and its flows
delete.description: Only while no testing day has ever been started from it; after that, results point at its snapshot and the answer is `PATCH { status: "archived" }`. Deleting drops the flows' marks, which can uncover tests.

409.description: A run exists for this template — archive it instead

get.summary: What this template covers, and what it misses
get.description: The 'covers 20 of 25 tests' line, and the list behind 'see what it misses'. A report, not a form.

get.summary: Devices a flow uses, and where each is introduced
get.description: Computed from the step list by @flowdeck/domain, the same function the editor and the runner use. Never stored: a hand-off banner is 'the first step using this device label', and storing it would make every insert and reorder a chance to leave a step orphaned above its own introduction.

200.description: Devices in order of first appearance

get.summary: Who this browser says it is

put.description: A name picker, not authentication. Seven people in one room, no roles, every change attributed.

get.summary: Names seen on this instance, for the picker

put.summary: Heartbeat: I am looking at this run / flow / template

get.summary: Testing days for a product, newest first

post.description: Takes a frozen snapshot of the template. Edits made during the day apply to the next run, never this one. Warns, via 409, if a run is already open for this template unless `force=true`.

409.description: A run is already open for this template

get.summary: Full run state: snapshot, flow runs, every result

post.description: Advisory, not exclusive. If someone already holds it, you get your own FlowRun alongside theirs and the response lists them, so the UI can ask 'Dana is on step 12 of 34 — run it anyway?' before this is called with confirm=true.

409.description: Already claimed by someone else; confirm to run alongside

post.summary: Abandon a flow — the next person starts from step 1

put.summary: Publish where you are in a flow you are running
put.description: Verdicts stay a draft on the tester's device until Finish, so an abandoned flow leaves nothing behind. This is the board's view of that draft while it lasts: the step the tester is on, a tally, and every non-pass with its note. Provisional — never counted in the day's numbers, and cleared on finish and abandon. Only the person who claimed the flow run can publish, and only while it is claimed.

409.description: Not a flow run you are running

post.summary: Record a verdict for one test on one step
post.description: Per test, not per step. Fail and skipped require a note. Idempotent on the client key. A blocking failure marks every later step in the flow as blocked; their tests report as not verified, never as failures.

404.description: No such flow run, step or test

delete.description: Removes one result and its attachments; the test reads as not verified on that step again. To change a verdict, record it again instead — the newer one replaces the older. This is for a result that should never have been recorded.
The step was fine after all, or its blocking report should stop blocking the rest of the flow.

post.summary: Pass every test a step marks, in one click
post.description: The common case stays as fast as the old per-step checkbox.

404.description: No such flow run or step

post.description: "The step, not the product": the button moved, the wording is stale, the screen is gone. Not a verdict — the tests the step marks can still be recorded. Either the tester got past it and `workaround` says how, or `blocking=true` closes the rest of the flow exactly as a blocking failure does. One report per step per flow run; flagging again replaces it.

404.description: No such flow run or step

post.summary: Attach an image to a result
post.description: Multipart: `file` (image), optional `width` and `height` from the client's own decode. Several per result are fine — before/after, both devices.

400.description: Not an image, or too large

get.summary: Images attached to a result
Disk used by attachments, against the budget

409.description: The ids are not exactly this template's flows — someone changed it under you

post.summary: Add a flow to a template

get.summary: A flow with its steps

patch.summary: Edit a flow's name, precondition or estimate, or archive it
patch.description: Archiving (`archived: true`) is the normal way to retire a flow: new testing days leave it out, its marks still count toward coverage, and days already started keep their snapshot. Set `archived: false` to bring it back.

delete.summary: Delete a flow and its steps
delete.description: Runs already started keep their snapshot, so nothing historical is lost. Marks vanish with the steps, which can uncover tests — the template page reports that.

post.summary: Insert a step at a position
post.description: Insert anywhere: the step takes the given index and what was there moves down. Hand-off banners are derived from order, so they follow automatically.

201.description: The new step and its transaction

patch.description: Last write wins per step. Changing kind to action drops the expected result.

put.description: The whole order in one transaction. Rejected unless the ids are exactly the flow's steps, which is what a drag against a flow someone else just edited looks like — the client re-syncs and the author drags again.

409.description: The ids are not exactly this flow's steps

put.summary: Mark a test on a step
put.description: Idempotent. The same test may be marked on any number of steps.

delete.summary: Unmark a test from a step

get.summary: Every step that marks this test
get.description: Answers 'if I change this, what am I affecting?', and gives the archive confirmation its numbers before anything happens.

get.summary: The issue feed: every non-pass result, self-contained
get.description: Typed `failure | minor | invalid_test`. Flowdeck does not filter — the adapter routes failures to the bug tracker and invalid tests to suite maintenance. Pass `includePass=true` for the whole day's data.

post.summary: Close a testing day (or reopen it)
post.description: Bookkeeping, not a lock: a closed run leaves the 'open days' list and its report is final. Flows still claimed are left as they are. `reopen=true` undoes it.

get.summary: One test over time
get.description: Every result ever recorded for the test, newest first, each against the version it ran against — a result from March stays readable against March's wording.

get.summary: The whole suite, as one document
get.description: Every test, template, flow and step, addressed by key. Archived templates and flows are included and say so; an archived test is included only while a step still verifies it. Keep `revision` — a push names it as `baseRevision`.

put.description: In one transaction. Matched by key: new keys are created, edited tests get a new version (the old one stays), and anything the document leaves out is archived — never deleted — so pushing it back restores it. Steps keep their ids where their content survives. Results already recorded are untouched: a testing day reads its own snapshot. Refused with 409 when the suite changed since `baseRevision`; pull again, or send `force`.

post.summary: What pushing this suite would change
post.description: Changes nothing. Lists each change (`+` created or restored, `~` edited, `-` archived) and the warnings. Errors — a bad key, a step verifying a test that does not exist — make it a 400 with each problem in `details`, by path.

post.summary: Bring a snapshot back, over a product or as a new one
post.description: `{ into: <product id or slug> }` pushes the snapshot over that product, forced: the product's suite becomes the snapshot's, and whatever the snapshot does not have is archived, never deleted. `{ into: "new", name? }` creates a product from it, named after the original unless `name` says otherwise.

200.description: What changed; `product` is the one it went into

400.description: The snapshot is not a valid suite

503.description: No backup bucket is configured (BACKUP_REPOSITORY and the S3 key pair)
